guide.title: The Roads Open Before the Unnumbered
guide.description: A continuous history from Ahn'Qiraj through Outland, Northrend, the Cataclysm, Pandaria, alternate Draenor, and the final campaign against the Burning Legion.

nodes.title: The great powers call upon unnumbered hands
nodes.narration: The age opened without a single crowned hero at its center. At Ahn'Qiraj, Alliance and Horde communities gathered a vast war effort while independent champions prepared to cross the opened gates. Their fellowship was temporary, their motives varied, and the atlas names them only as adventurers: an interpretive company standing for the many who entered dangers that armies alone had not resolved.

nodes.title: The road crosses into a broken world
nodes.narration: The Dark Portal opened again, and the chronicle changed its ground. Outland was not a distant province on Azeroth's sea, but the remains of Draenor under another sky. The atlas therefore closes one worldspace and opens another. Across that shattered land, old exiles, demonic powers, and new expeditions met within consequences already centuries in the making.

nodes.title: The northern crown receives its reckoning
nodes.narration: The next great campaign returned to Azeroth and climbed through Northrend toward Icecrown. Arthas had once crossed this cold seeking the strength to save his kingdom; now others followed the ruin of that choice to its throne. The stages shown are strategic memory, not a raid plan. At the citadel's height, the Lich King's reign ended, though the burdens bound to Northrend did not vanish with him.

nodes.title: The earth remembers its betrayed guardian
nodes.narration: Then Deathwing returned, and the land itself became testimony. Coasts broke, mountains opened, and old regions entered a new state that could not honestly be shown as a mere overlay upon yesterday. The scarred terrain before you is interpretive rather than surveyed. Its purpose is to make one consequence unmistakable: Azeroth after the Cataclysm was not the same world the northern victors had left behind.

nodes.title: A hidden land receives an old quarrel
nodes.narration: Beyond the Cataclysm's upheaval, Pandaria returned to the wider world's knowledge. Its peoples and landscapes were not an empty stage awaiting foreign banners. Yet Alliance and Horde carried their rivalry ashore, and the consequences deepened within a land that had long endured histories of its own. The atlas holds Pandaria as a place encountered, not discovered into existence by those who arrived from elsewhere.

nodes.title: The war turns upon its own warchief
nodes.narration: The conflict carried home from Pandaria did not leave the Horde whole. Opposition to Garrosh's rule gathered within it while Alliance forces advanced upon Orgrimmar. Their purposes met in a siege that ended his leadership, not in a simple reconciliation of every grievance. The city marker is only a narrative anchor; the greater change was political, dividing obedience from belonging and leaving another unsettled road ahead.

nodes.title: History opens beside itself
nodes.narration: The next invasion came from an alternate Draenor: neither the intact world remembered in earlier centuries nor the Outland made by its destruction. Iron and ambition had formed the Iron Horde there. A separate worldspace keeps that distinction visible. This terrain is an interpretive echo of unbroken Draenor, while the anonymous war host represents an embodied power rather than any one named commander or exact camp.

nodes.title: The ancient enemy returns to the Broken Isles
nodes.narration: From the alternate war's ending rose the way for an older enemy to return. The Burning Legion invaded through the Broken Isles. Established armies could not answer every wound, and distinct class orders gathered champions according to calling rather than kingdom. The ensemble before you is symbolic: many orders, many traditions, one immediate necessity. Beside them stood Illidan, carrying his own long and perilous history into the defense.

nodes.title: The defenders carry the war to Argus
nodes.narration: Defense became pursuit, and pursuit crossed the dark between worlds. Argus appears in its own atlas measure: a shattered realm of broken plateaus and fel-lit wounds, rendered as interpretive terrain rather than surveyed fact. There old exiles, the Army of the Light, Illidan, and Azeroth's champions struck at the Legion's seat. No geographic line joins the worlds; the change of state tells the crossing honestly.

nodes.title: Victory returns to a wounded world
nodes.narration: The Legion's immediate crusade was broken on Argus, and the age of far roads reached its sternest victory. Yet those roads led home to no untouched morning. Azeroth had endured the Scourge, the Cataclysm, faction war, and powers from beyond its sky. The champions who had crossed so many thresholds returned to a world whose wounds would become causes in their own right—and whose next war would begin before healing was complete.
